subject: Food Science
title: Louis Pasteur's Revolution
description: A fast breakdown of Louis Pasteur's Revolution for builders.

hook.text: French wine producers were losing millions to spoiled wine. They hired Louis Pasteur in 1863.

buildup.text: Louis Pasteur's Revolution sets up the core claim, the assumptions, and the stakes.

discovery.text: He showed that heating wine to 55°C killed spoilage bacteria without ruining flavor.

twist.text: Pasteur was a chemist, not a doctor. His germ theory was rejected by the medical establishment for years.

climax.text: Louis Pasteur's Revolution matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: Sour wine led to germ theory. Germ theory led to food safety.

quiz.question: What originally motivated Pasteur's discovery of pasteurization?
options: French wine producers losing money to spoiled wine
